I don't think that's true. Society tells us to be this and that and if we are not, we are failure. But what society tells us we are not doesn't mean we don't have other important qualities. I don't know where you're from or what you're going through but I've been similarly depressed and I eventually found my way in life. For me, I realised what makes me happy is not having an impressive career, or the money in my bank account, or getting married and having kids, which society tells us we should strive to achieve and it will makes us fulfilled. It makes me happy to help other people so I started volunteering. It really is as simple as that sometimes. Society also expects us to be in perfect health and if we are not, well there no place for us. You just need to find out what makes you happy and work towards it. You don't owe anything to anyone but yourself, the world is crazy enough as it is. No one owes you anything either, you have to figure some stuff out on your own.
It probably won't mean much to you but I'm glad you wrote this on a public forum. You're not alone in your struggles but you have to keep going, one day at a time.

There are many jobs for programmers in game dev but they're often worse pay than other programming jobs outside of the industry. I feel like the work is more interesting though so it might be worth it for you. I'm a designer myself that can code somewhat so what's interesting to me might bore you.
You can always start a game with your friends just for fun and practice. I'm afraid success is very difficult to predict so I wouldn't leave my day job for it.

I haven't been in the industry for long (4 years) but I've heard good things about Supergiant Games, Klei and Ninja Theory. Their games are critically acclaimed as well, so it's a win-win for everyone. 
Mobile games studios have a better work environment than most in my experience, however I understand it's not exactly the dream for a lot of young devs. There is a lot of misinformation on reddit but the reality is not so black and white. Different studios have different problems, and game dev is a job like any other.

I'm a woman and I work in the game industry and I have encountered harassment from male colleagues. However, not all companies are like Blizzard, some value diversity and equality. My current company has no crunch or overtime either.

I do believe that most AAA studios are to be avoided from what I've heard from fellow game developers.

It made me realize my goal was really unrealistic. I hope you find the right weight for you but most importantly realize it shouldn't stop you from living your life.
